reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a $200 BitConnect giveaway, presents the benefit as guaranteed, and asks interested viewers to click a description link and invest $100. It also requires signing up with Serg007 as sponsor and replying with a video showing that sponsor before further information is provided, although the records do not establish what the link leads to or whether any payment or reward was completed.

citations.quote: click on the link in the description, invest $100 into your BitConnect and I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%
Yo, free $200.
Free $200 Bitconnect give away!!
Click link sign up with Serg007 as sponsor

opening.argument: Judge, the wording does not support treating this as a demonstrated fraudulent payout scheme. The speaker addresses only viewers who are interested and promises to send information on how to get the $200, rather than saying a payment has already been made. The phrase "guaranteed 100%" is strong promotional language, but the record does not show the terms behind it or whether anyone received or lost money. The observed pitch can still be read as an offer whose details are disclosed later, not proof that the offer is false.

citations.quote: If you're interested, click on the link in the description, invest $100 into your BitConnect and I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%.
Free $200 Bitconnect give away!!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker uses a guarantee, but its quotes establish a promise to provide information on how to get $200, not a completed transfer or a proven false claim. The description likewise says the speaker will DM further information. Neither quote supplies the missing terms or an outcome, so those points alone do not settle whether the advertised giveaway is fraudulent.

citations.quote: I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%.
I will dm with info on how to receive ...

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a documented loss does not neutralize the solicitation. The speaker directs viewers to invest $100 into BitConnect as part of getting information on a supposedly guaranteed $200 benefit. There is no disclaimer or risk warning in the supplied text to qualify that guarantee; the conditional phrase merely identifies the viewers being solicited.

citations.quote: If you're interested, click on the link in the description, invest $100 into your BitConnect and I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%.

opening.argument: Judge, a narrower reading is that this short video introduces a process whose actual instructions will be provided afterward. The speaker says he will send "info on how to get" the $200, and the description asks for a reply showing the named sponsor before that DM. Those are procedural steps, while the supplied material contains no demonstration of a payout, account balance, or realized return. The promise deserves scrutiny, but the record leaves the content of the promised instructions unseen.

citations.quote: I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%.
reply with video showing serg007 as sponsor and I will dm with info on how to receive ...

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes a call to invest, and that is a serious point. But it also describes the $200 as a benefit tied to that investment without access to the later DM explaining the claimed process. The sponsor-verification request can be read as a step for identifying eligible participants; by itself, it does not show what happens after someone replies.

citations.quote: invest $100 into your BitConnect and I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%.
reply with video showing serg007 as sponsor and I will dm with info on how to receive ...

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promising instructions later does not make the visible message educational. The visible instruction is to click a link and invest $100, followed by a claim about getting $200 "guaranteed 100%." The description adds sponsor sign-up and verification. The unseen DM cannot undo the solicitation already made in the supplied material.

citations.quote: click on the link in the description, invest $100 into your BitConnect and I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%.
Click link sign up with Serg007 as sponsor reply with video showing serg007 as sponsor

opening.argument: Judge, the most concrete mechanism visible here is a sponsor-linked promotion. The title calls it a giveaway, and the description asks viewers to sign up with Serg007 as sponsor and show that sponsor in a reply. The speaker does tell interested viewers to invest $100 and uses an unequivocal guarantee, but the supplied record does not show where the link goes, who receives the $100, or how the $200 would be funded. It is therefore possible to read the offer as a referral reward contingent on participation, without assuming an unseen diversion of funds.

citations.quote: Free $200 Bitconnect give away!!
Click link sign up with Serg007 as sponsor reply with video showing serg007 as sponsor
invest $100 into your BitConnect and I will send you the info on how to get the $200 guaranteed 100%.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's investment quote establishes that $100 participation is requested, but it does not establish that the speaker collects that money. Its sponsor quote establishes a referral condition, not a downline-income promise or a request for account credentials. The missing link destination and reward terms matter when deciding whether this is a deceptive scheme rather than an ordinary, if aggressively worded, promotion.

citations.quote: click on the link in the description, invest $100 into your BitConnect
sign up with Serg007 as sponsor reply with video showing serg007 as sponsor

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A referral structure does not remove the central concern: viewers are told to invest $100 into BitConnect to obtain information on getting $200, advertised as guaranteed. The title's giveaway framing and the sponsor-sign-up requirement reinforce the inducement. Direct collection by the speaker, credential theft, and a completed loss are not necessary to identify the investment-linked promise being promoted.
